title: Hotel Manager Salary: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay for a 38-Hour Week
description: Learn how to convert a hotel manager salary from hourly to annual using a 38-hour week, including award rates, tax, and super. Use our timesheet tool.
salarySummary: For a hotel manager under the Hospitality Award, the minimum annual salary is $63,617 based on a 38-hour week, but salary absorption may apply if paid at least 125% of that amount.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hotel manager salary under the Hospitality Award?
faqs.a: The Hospitality Industry (General) Award 2020 sets a minimum annual salary of $63,617 for Managerial Staff (Hotels) as of 1 July 2026. This is based on a 38-hour full-time week. If the manager is paid at least 125% of this minimum ($79,521.25), the employer may use salary absorption to cover penalty rates, overtime, and allowances.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly hotel manager rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, an hourly rate of $35.00 gives $35.00 × 38 × 52 = $69,160 per year. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime or penalty rates. Use [the timesheet](/) to do the calculation.

faqs.q: Does the hotel manager salary include superannuation?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of the salary. The super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). For a hotel manager earning $70,000, the employer would contribute an additional $8,400 per year into the super fund. This is separate from the salary figure.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Annual Pay Formula

Converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is straightforward: multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52 weeks. For full-time employees under most awards, including the Hospitality Industry (General) Award 2020, the standard is 38 ordinary hours per week.

**Formula:** Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks.

For example, a **hotel manager salary** quoted at $35.00 per hour would be $35.00 × 38 × 52 = $69,160 per year. This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. It also excludes superannuation, which is paid on top.

To see the fortnightly equivalent, multiply the weekly amount by 2. Using the same example, weekly pay is $1,330.00, so fortnightly pay is $2,660.00 before tax.

## Hotel Manager Salary Under the Hospitality Award

Hotel managers performing lower-level duties are covered by the Hospitality Industry (General) Award 2020. The award sets a minimum annual salary of $63,617 for Managerial Staff (Hotels) as of 1 July 2026. This is based on a 38-hour week.

However, clause 25 of the award allows for salary absorption. If the hotel manager is paid at least 125% of the minimum annual salary (i.e., $79,521.25), the employer can absorb penalty rates, overtime, allowances, and breaks into that salary. This means the manager does not receive those additional payments separately. The Fair Work Ombudsman notes that this requirement does not involve comparing the salary to what the employee would otherwise be paid under the award.

For a hotel manager earning above the absorption threshold, the annual salary is a fixed amount that covers all ordinary hours and additional work. To convert that annual salary back to an hourly rate, divide by 52 weeks and then by 38 hours. For example, $80,000 per year gives $80,000 ÷ 52 ÷ 38 ≈ $40.49 per hour.

## National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual rate $33.05 per hour. However, hotel managers are classified under a different part of the award and are not paid at the minimum wage rate. The award provides specific minimum rates for various roles, but managerial staff have their own salary structure.

When comparing a **hotel manager salary** to other hospitality roles, remember that managers are typically salaried and may not receive penalty rates or overtime if salary absorption applies. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has more details on base rates.

## Tax and Superannuation

Once you have the annual gross salary, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

A Medicare levy of 2% generally applies (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as a guide). For a hotel manager earning $80,000, the tax estimate would be:

- $0 on first $18,200
- 15% on $26,800 ($18,201–$45,000) = $4,020
- 30% on $35,000 ($45,001–$80,000) = $10,500
- Total tax = $14,520
- Medicare levy (2% of $80,000) = $1,600
- Net income after tax and Medicare ≈ $63,880

Superannuation is paid on top of the salary. The super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). For a $80,000 salary, the employer contributes an additional $9,600 per year. This is not deducted from your salary; it is an extra benefit. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Using the Timesheet

Our [timesheet](/) tool lets you enter an hourly rate and see the annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly equivalents. A checkbox adds 25% casual loading on top of the base rate—do not enter a rate that already includes loading. The tool uses the same formula: hourly × hours per week × 52, with a default of 38 hours. You can adjust the hours if your role differs.

For hotel managers, the timesheet can help you check whether a salary offer matches the hourly equivalent of the award minimum. Remember that salary absorption may mean your annual salary already includes allowances and overtime, so the hourly rate derived from the salary may be lower than the award hourly rate for non-managerial staff.

For more detailed award rates, see our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data). The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page provides broader industry benchmarks.

**Disclaimer:** Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
